[CrOS] Load Image Loader component extension on demand

Instead of loading the Image Loader component extension at login in
AddDefaultComponentExtensionsWithBackgroundPages() (which spins up a
~20 MiB ServiceWorker process even when unused), load it on demand in
its only two callers: Files app (ChromeFileManagerUIDelegate) and
ash::ThumbnailLoader.

[Test] Disable remaining collapsed AccountPickerBottomSheetRenderTests

All testCollapsedSheet* methods in AccountPickerBottomSheetRenderTest
race with initial Edge-to-Edge bottom gesture navigation bar inset
delivery right after startOnBlankPage(), causing the bottom sheet view
height to alternate nondeterministically between 1818px and 1746px in
Skia Gold. Disabling the remaining three collapsed-sheet render tests
stops CQ shard flakiness while the underlying root-view LayoutParams and
inset synchronization are fixed.

[cronet gn2bp] Fix host toolchain Crubit target resolution

When a `cpp_api_from_rust` target is built for a non-default toolchain
(such as the Linux host toolchain when `//base` depends on a Crubit
target), `gn desc` appends the `(<toolchain>)` suffix to all dependency
labels in `deps`, while `metadata["rust_target"]` stores the
toolchain-less label (`label_no_toolchain`).

This caused two issues in `GnParser.parse_gn_desc`:
1. `d.endswith(("_crubit_action", "_crubit_impl", "_crubit_rspgen"))`
   failed to strip the toolchain suffix before checking the target name,
   allowing `_crubit_impl(<toolchain>)` (a raw `rust_library` without
   `rustenv`) to be traversed and fail with `KeyError: 'rustenv'`.
2. `metadata["rust_target"][0]` resolved to the default Android
   toolchain target rather than the matching host toolchain target,
   wiring the host `crubit_cpp_from_rust` module to the device
   `rust_ffi_static` module and dropping its host `rustlibs`.

Strip the toolchain via `label_without_toolchain` when filtering
internal `_crubit_*` subtargets and propagate any non-default toolchain
suffix onto `rust_target_label`.

[cronet gn2bp] Use source_subdir for Crubit

Previously, gn2bp generated a companion `<name>__headers` `cc_genrule`
for each `crubit_cpp_from_rust` module to copy the generated crate
header to its GN `root_gen_dir`-relative path and emit forwarding
headers for `third_party/crubit/support/rs_std/rs_{core,alloc,std}.h`.

Now that Soong's `crubit_cpp_from_rust` supports the `source_subdir`
property, re-exports Crubit stdlib headers with `source_subdir:
"third_party/crubit/support/rs_std"` and `source_stem:
"rs_{core,alloc,std}"` to C++ consumers, and uses `.h` for generated
headers, the companion `__headers` `cc_genrule` is no longer needed.

Set `source_subdir` directly on `CrubitModule` and remove the companion
`cc_genrule` generation.

Glic: Take the browser window as JniPtr in toggleUI

GlicKeyedService#toggleUI() takes the native BrowserWindowInterface as a
raw long, which GlicKeyedServiceHandler obtains from ChromeAndroidTask
and glic_keyed_service_android.cc casts back with reinterpret_cast. The
long is detached from the JniUniquePtr through which
AndroidBrowserWindow owns the native window, so nothing stops a stale
value from reaching C++ as a dangling pointer.

Make toggleUI() take JniPtr<NativeBrowserWindowInterface>, obtained from
ChromeAndroidTask#getNativeBrowserWindow() added in
https://crrev.com/c/8620634, so that JNI Zero hands
BrowserWindowInterface* to C++ directly. Behavior is unchanged, except
that passing a destroyed window to native now throws
IllegalStateException in Java instead of using freed memory.

UI: Migrate AcceleratorManager to JniUniquePtr

AcceleratorManager stores its native ::ui::AcceleratorManagerAndroid
address in a raw Java long field. Passing untyped integer handles across
the JNI boundary bypasses compile-time type checking and ownership
enforcement.

Declare a package-private NativeAcceleratorManagerAndroid JniTypeToken
mapped to ::ui::AcceleratorManagerAndroid and hold the Java-owned peer
in a JniUniquePtr<NativeAcceleratorManagerAndroid> allocated via
jni_zero::MakeUnique. Pass the handle to @NativeMethods calls using
JniPtr<NativeAcceleratorManagerAndroid> and destroy the native peer via
destroy().

PaymentManifestDownloader: Adopt JniUniquePtr

PaymentManifestDownloader stores its native
::payments::PaymentManifestDownloaderAndroid pointer in raw long field
mNativeObject. Passing raw integer handles across the JNI boundary
bypasses type checking and smart pointer lifecycle enforcement, risking
use-after-free bugs if the native object is accessed after destruction.

Migrate mNativeObject to JniUniquePtr with a package-private
JniTypeToken mapped to ::payments::PaymentManifestDownloaderAndroid via
@JniType. Return jni_zero::MakeUnique from the C++ factory, destroy the
owned instance via JniUniquePtr.destroy(), and pass JniPtr to
@NativeMethods calls.

NTP: Adopt JniRawPtr in CrossDeviceThemeTracker

Replace the raw long mNativePtr field in CrossDeviceThemeTracker with
JniRawPtr so JNI Zero tracks the borrowed reference to
::themes::CrossDeviceThemeTrackerAndroid with BackupRefPtr protection
across JNI calls.

Pass jni_zero::MakeRaw(this) when constructing the Java peer and invoke
JniRawPtr.release() inside clearNativePtr() when the C++ owner detaches.
Subsequent native calls hit the null guard exactly like the old 0 guard.

BrowserWindow: Return the created window as JniPtr

BrowserWindowCreatorBridge#createBrowserWindow() returns the native
BrowserWindowInterface of the new window as a raw long, and
create_browser_window_android.cc casts it back with reinterpret_cast.
The long is detached from the JniUniquePtr through which
AndroidBrowserWindow owns the native window.

Return JniPtr<NativeBrowserWindowInterface> from
ChromeAndroidTask#getOrCreateNativeBrowserWindow(), added in
https://crrev.com/c/8620634, with null where 0 was returned, so that JNI
Zero hands BrowserWindowInterface* to C++ directly and the cast goes
away. Behavior is unchanged.

🌺 Disable 2 consistently failing tests

The following tests failed all retry attempts (hard-failed) in 4/20
recent builds on android-14-arm64-rel-tests.

Disabled here:
  TabbedNavigationBarColorControllerTest.testNavBarColorAnimationsEdgeToEdgeBottomChin (all platforms)
  TabbedNavigationBarColorControllerTest.testNavBarColorAnimationsEdgeToEdgeEverywhere (all platforms)

Example failing run:
https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/chrome/builders/ci/android-14-arm64-rel-tests/5389

Why disable rather than revert:
Fails with AssertionError (expected Color.BLUE <-16776961> but was
Color.WHITE <-1>) in testNavBarColorAnimations() because
spyEdgeToEdgeSystemBarColorHelper is injected and cleared on the
instrumentation thread without ThreadUtils.runOnUiThreadBlocking while
the initial tab background color update to Color.WHITE (-1) is still in
flight on the UI thread.

To run/deflake this test on CQ before re-enabling, add the following
footer(s) to your CL description:
  Include-Ci-Only-Tests: internal.client.clank:android-14-arm64-rel-tests|chrome_public_test_apk

This is mitigation, not a fix. The bug tracks the real investigation and
is assigned to the owning team.

🌺 Filter FeedV2NewTabPageTest#testNavigateBackToNTPWithFeeds on android-code-coverage

FeedV2NewTabPageTest#testNavigateBackToNTPWithFeeds has hard-failed in 8
consecutive builds (#8155-#8162) on chromium/ci/android-code-coverage
(Pixel 2, Android 10 Q, Java coverage instrumentation), and is the sole
remaining test failure on the builder after recent fixes.

In testNavigateBackToNTPWithFeeds, scrolling to MIN_ITEMS_AFTER_LOAD (10)
triggers FeedStream#maybeLoadMore (appending a LoadingSpinnerSlice at
index 12). Under full-shard JaCoCo coverage overhead on Pixel 2, when
navigating back to the NTP, LinearLayoutManager#fixLayoutEndGap adjusts
the top visible item above mPositionToRestore, leaving
getRestoringStateSupplier() at WAITING_TO_RESTORE (0) until timeout.

The test is already disabled on Android > Q via @DisableIf.Build. Filter
it on android-code-coverage via
android.code_coverage.chrome_public_test_apk.filter so it continues to
run on android-10-x86-rel while unblocking android-code-coverage.

Glic: Take the browser window as JniPtr in split button

GlicSplitButtonDelegateBridge reads the native BrowserWindowInterface
from InitInfo as a raw long and glic_split_button_delegate_android.cc
casts it back with reinterpret_cast. The long is detached from the
JniUniquePtr through which AndroidBrowserWindow owns the native window,
so nothing stops a stale value from reaching C++ as a dangling pointer.

Read InitInfo#nativeBrowserWindow, added in https://crrev.com/c/8620634,
and declare the native parameter as JniPtr<NativeBrowserWindowInterface>
so that JNI Zero hands BrowserWindowInterface* to C++ directly. Behavior
is unchanged, except that passing a destroyed window to native now
throws IllegalStateException in Java instead of using freed memory.

parent
4771b3cb39efa2ad8c0f628e651df5e22a36b08e [ diff ] 
BrowserWindow: Add JniPtr accessors for the native window

ChromeAndroidTask and ChromeAndroidTaskFeature.InitInfo hand the native
BrowserWindowInterface to features only as a raw long. Since
https://crrev.com/c/8456082, AndroidBrowserWindow owns that object
through a JniUniquePtr, but a long copied out of it is detached from
that lifecycle: a feature that keeps or forwards the value after the
window is destroyed passes a dangling address to C++, and every bridge
has to reinterpret_cast it back.

Add JniPtr<NativeBrowserWindowInterface> variants next to the long API:
ChromeAndroidTask#getOrCreateNativeBrowserWindow(),
ChromeAndroidTask#getNativeBrowserWindow() and
InitInfo#nativeBrowserWindow, with null where the long API uses 0. They
return the JniPtr owned by the AndroidBrowserWindow that backs the long
values, and the long and JniPtr getters share the window lookup, so both
variants always refer to the same window. Once the window is destroyed,
passing the JniPtr to native throws IllegalStateException in Java
instead of using freed memory.

The long API stays so that each feature can switch to the JniPtr
variant in its own CL. It will be removed once no callers remain.
Existing callers are unaffected.

Tests for in-flight probe alongside additional migration

Previously, tests where an additional migration occurred, while a probe
was already in flight (e.g.,
ProbingFailsWithNoUnusedConnectionIdWhenProbingInFlight) could only
verify the second migration failed with kNoUnusedConnectionId, because
the client defaulted to active_connection_id_limit = 2 (only 1 spare
CID).

Now that configuring a higher active_connection_id_limit is supported
via connection options (k3CID) and the quic_active_connection_id_limit
flag, add tests in QuicSessionPoolTest with multiple spare connection
IDs.

[composebox] Streamline FuseboxAction state and selection lifecycle

Previously, `handleFuseboxAction()` and
`executeSuggestionFuseboxAction_()` relied on `updateStateComplete_` and
multiple sequential `updateComplete` awaits across Lit render cycles:

1. For `QueryActionOverride.kPaste`, `handleFuseboxAction()` awaited
three consecutive promises after setting `this.state` before calling
`selectAll()`.

2. For `QueryActionOverride.kHint`, `handleFuseboxAction()` populated
`state.text` with the hint string, and
`executeSuggestionFuseboxAction_()` awaited multiple render cycles to
restore `this.input` back to `originalInput`. Simplify the lifecycle by
handling `QueryActionOverride.kHint` in `handleFuseboxAction()` without
overwriting `state.text`, allowing
`maybeHandleSuggestionFuseboxAction_()` to invoke
`handleFuseboxAction()` directly and removing
`executeSuggestionFuseboxAction_()`.

3. Move post-update input selection into the end of `updateState()` via
`selectAllOnStateUpdate_`, removing `updateStateComplete_`.

Manually checked the flow in composebox still worked as expected (Tool
Mode, Model Mode, etc):
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTYyODIzNTQ4NzM3OTQ1NnxiMjljNTBlMy00YQ

942720c3bae4aa25e852d7cc280cbbcd8ffc0c7b [ diff ] 
[ntp-composebox] Set composebox state imperatively on open

Previously, `<ntp-app>` stored `composeboxState_` and bound it via
`.state="${this.composeboxState_}"` on `<ntp-composebox>`. When
`<ntp-composebox>` subsequently updated its own `state` internally (for
example via `handleFuseboxAction()` when selecting an image suggestion),
`<ntp-composebox>.state` diverged from `<ntp-app>.composeboxState_`. Any
later `<ntp-app>` re-render (such as `focusout`/`focusin` on
`#searchboxContainer` when dismissing the tool chip) caused Lit to
re-assign the stale `composeboxState_` back to `<ntp-composebox>`,
re-triggering `updateState()` and re-enabling the cleared tool mode.
Remove `composeboxState_` and the `.state` template binding from
`<ntp-app>`, and instead make `ensureComposeboxOpen_()` async then
assign `composebox.state` imperatively in `openComposebox_()` after
`ensureComposeboxOpen_()`.

Screencast of the issue:
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NDkzOTI5MzYwNzg1NDA4MHw0NWZjNzJlOC0xYw

Screencast of the fix:
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTg0MDQ0MzI0NDgwNjE0NHxlMGJhYzU1ZS03Nw

webnn: Serialize CoreML on context sequence

Previously, ContextImplCoreml ran on the GPU main thread while
dispatching MLModel predictions asynchronously via ResourceTask and
loading MLModel instances on background worker threads.

To simplify, move ContextImplCoreml onto a dedicated
SingleThreadTaskRunner, matching the ORT and LiteRT backends. Load
MLModel, execute predictions synchronously via -[MLModel
predictionFromFeatures:options:error:], and release MLModel within
@autoreleasepool blocks on the context sequence. Since all graph
dispatches and tensor reads/writes are now serialized by the context's
GPU sequence, remove ResourceTask, QueueableResourceState, and
BufferContent usage from the CoreML backend.

[base] Avoid temporary string allocation in IsSwitchNameValid()

IsSwitchNameValid() is called in DCHECK on CommandLine::HasSwitch() and
CommandLine::GetSwitchValueNative() calls. ToLowerASCII(switch_name)
materializes a temporary std::string copy on the heap whenever
switch_name.size() > 22 (exceeding libc++ SSO) just to compare it
against switch_name.

Use std::ranges::none_of(switch_name, &IsAsciiUpper<char>) to validate
that switch names are lowercase ASCII in-place without heap allocations.

0e5576a8adf7a11c047214fa7ece91677fdfe595 [ diff ] 
ash: Migrate SystemTrayClientImpl off //chrome/browser/ui/navigator

Add `ignore_path_for_tab_reuse` to `BrowserController::OpenUrlParams`
and use `BrowserController::OpenUrl` in `SystemTrayClientImpl` instead
of `ShowSingletonTab` and `ShowSingletonTabOverwritingNTP`.

Minor behavior changes for the sake of interface simplicity:

Previously, the code only looked for an existing tab in the most
recently active tabbed browser. With `BrowserController::OpenUrl`, it
instead searches across all of the user's browser windows, avoiding
duplicate Calendar or Help tabs when one is already open in another
window. In addition, when `ShowPaletteHelp` opens a new tab, it no
longer sets the previously active tab as the opener, which happens to be
more appropriate for an OS-initiated navigation.

[NTP Customization Sync] Recreate the Activity on a synced theme change

An Activity computes its dynamic colors from the persisted NTP theme
when it is created, while a Chrome color or hex color theme is
initialized in NtpCustomizationConfigManager lazily, when the first NTP
listener registers. On tablets nothing registers before the NTP is
shown, but the synced themes are replayed as soon as native is
initialized, so a synced theme can replace the persisted theme before
the initialization. The initialization then reads the synced theme as
the active one, maybeApplyBackgroundUpdateFromDeviceSync() finds no
mismatch between the active and the staged theme, and the Activity keeps
the colors of the previous theme.

The synced theme handlers now record that they replaced the persisted
theme, and maybeApplyBackgroundUpdateFromDeviceSync() applies the staged
theme and recreates the Activity based on that record instead of
comparing the staged theme with the active one. The record is in memory
on purpose: after a restart the Activity starts from the replaced
SharedPreferences, so nothing is stale and nothing needs to be applied.
A local theme selection drops the record together with the staged theme,
since it recreates the Activity itself.

[Webium] Use the user profile for favicons in TopChromeWebUIProfile

With kTopChromeWebUISharedRenderer flag, the WebUI toolbar will be
created in TopChromeWebUIProfile (crrev.com/c/8429343), which hosts the
Top Chrome WebUIs of the windows of all profiles in shared renderer
processes. It has no history or favicons of its own.

Design doc:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1jTJ4rAlNMS6aKZtfSdKh61sVWq9M6-XQfHKjNsoa4dU/edit?usp=sharing

The toolbar requests chrome://favicon2, e.g. for the drag image of the
URL in its location bar. A URLDataSource is registered per
BrowserContext and host, so the toolbars of all windows will share one
FaviconSource there, which can't hold the profile of a window. Instead,
the profile has to be decided per request, from the requesting
WebContents.

A FaviconSource created for TopChromeWebUIProfile now serves the
favicons of the user profile of the requesting contents. Callers, e.g.
WebUIToolbarUI, pass the profile of the WebUI as before.

No behavior change, since no WebUI is in TopChromeWebUIProfile yet.

[navigation] Match MHTML MIME types case-insensitively in the browser

Per RFC 2045 Section 5.1, media types and subtypes are case-insensitive.
However, browser process MHTML classification in
NavigationRequest::IsMhtmlMimeType(), download_utils::MustDownload(),
and IntentHandler.isMhtmlMimeType() used exact, case-sensitive string
equality for "multipart/related" and "message/rfc822". Meanwhile,
non-HTTP loaders like Android's ContentURLLoader forwarded unnormalized
MIME types from ContentProvider.getType().

Implement UDIF parsing part 1 (ParseBlkx, ParseBlockData)

This CL implements a portion of UDIF parsing in Rust, specifically
mirroring UDIFParser::{Parse, GetNumberOfPartitions, GetPartitionName,
GetPartitionType, ParseBlkx}.

This port intentionally mirrors the C++ approach of casting the raw
bytes to struct types (see usage of base::BufferIterator in C++) by
using the bytemuck crate to (safely) do the same with the equivalent
Rust types. All struct fields are subsequently converted from big-endian
to host-native representation.

Note that the original C++ relies on several CoreFoundation libraries to
do the XML/PList parsing, which we replicate somewhat by hand in Rust
(using the xml and base64 crates).

parent
1f4f7d983a5106cd8c56776e371b597db5c977ab [ diff ] 
[MemoryCoordinator] Don't send release requests to passive consumers

Passive consumers can't release memory: PassiveMemoryConsumer's
OnReleaseMemory() is a final no-op. Still, release requests were sent to
them, which caused needless IPCs, consumer fan-out and posted tasks
(e.g. for AsyncMemoryConsumerRegistration).

MemoryCoordinatorPolicyManager now clears the release flag for passive
consumer groups, which drops release-only updates entirely while still
delivering memory limit changes.

[gc] Defer CalculationValue handle decrements from ~Length()

`~Length()` may execute during GC sweeping is occurring, and touching
heap objects is disallowed.

Make `CalculationValueHandleMap` queue these decrements into a
non-Oilpan `Vector` to be flushed on subsequent map insert/Increment
operations.

[CrOS] Lazily launch Quick Answers SpellCheckService on demand

SpellCheckLanguage::Initialize() eagerly launches the
quick_answers.mojom.SpellCheckService utility process (~6.8 MB PSS) and
loads the Hunspell dictionary on login whenever Quick Answers is
enabled, even if the user never right-clicks or selects text to trigger
Quick Answers.

Defer launching the SpellCheckService process and loading the dictionary
until CheckSpelling() is called.

Bug: b:575247202
Test: Verified in Task Manager that the service is not started at login and launches on demand when using Quick Answers

e9e42b9bf8fe31abc7ddb04ccd30824a5c4c1743 [ diff ] 
webnn: Avoid 32-bit overflow when reading or writing MLMultiArray

When an MLMultiArray is backed by an IOSurface/CVPixelBuffer with row
padding (such as a large float16 tensor with height 47,267,220 and 128
bytes per row), the leading dimension stride (e.g. 3,025,102,080
elements) multiplied by `item_byte_size` (2 bytes) exceeds `UINT32_MAX`
(6,050,204,160 bytes).

Previously, `GetDataTypeByteSize()`, `ToStdVector()`,
`RecursivelyReadFromMLMultiArray()`, and
`RecursivelyWriteToMLMultiArray()` in `utils_coreml.mm` used `uint32_t`
for `item_byte_size`, `shape`, and `strides`. Consequently, `strides[0]
* item_byte_size` overflowed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic and wrapped
around modulo 2^32 (to 1,755,236,864 bytes) before widening to `size_t`,
passing a truncated subspan to the recursive call and triggering
`CHECK(input_subspan)` or `CHECK(output_subspan)`.

Change `GetDataTypeByteSize()`, `ToStdVector()`,
`RecursivelyReadFromMLMultiArray()`, and
`RecursivelyWriteToMLMultiArray()` to use `size_t` and
`base::CheckMul()` for byte-size calculations.

[🌷] Disable BookmarkSaveFlowTest#testBookmarkSaveFlow_WithShoppingListItem on Android 16

BookmarkSaveFlowTest#testBookmarkSaveFlow_WithShoppingListItem is
flaking at >10% (2 of 18 builds, 11.1%) on android-16-x64-dbg-tests.
BookmarkSaveFlowCoordinator#show requests the bottom sheet
asynchronously, and the test invokes RenderTestRule#render before
waiting for the sheet to open and window insets to settle, producing
inconsistent view heights in Skia Gold comparisons.

[Bookmarks Bar] Re-enable BookmarkBarCoordinatorTest constructor tests

Re-enables `testConstructorWhenTopControlOffsetIsNonZero` and
`testConstructorWhenTopControlOffsetIsZero` in
`BookmarkBarCoordinatorTest`.

Both tests were disabled in crrev.com/c/6841987 when
`BrowserControlsStateProvider` was moved from `BookmarkBarMediator` to
`BookmarkBarCoordinator`, temporarily removing the constructor
initialization of the bookmark bar view's top margin and visibility
while `BookmarkBarSceneLayer` was being added.

Subsequently, crrev.com/c/7124355 updated the `BookmarkBarCoordinator`
constructor to initialize the view's top margin from
`TopControlsStacker#getHeightFromLayerToTop` for `BOOKMARK_BAR` instead
of `BrowserControlsStateProvider#getTopControlsHeight()`, and
crrev.com/c/7995497 updated the constructor to initialize the Android
widget visibility via `updateAndroidWidgetVisibility()`.

Because `testConstructor` still stubbed
`mBrowserControlsManager.getTopControlsHeight()` and asserted
`topControlsHeight - mView.getHeight()` as the top margin, the top
margin assertion failed when the tests were re-enabled because
`mTopControlsStacker.getHeightFromLayerToTop` returned 0 instead of
`topControlsHeight`. Update `testConstructor` to stub
`mTopControlsStacker.getHeightFromLayerToTop` for `BOOKMARK_BAR` and
assert `topControlsHeight` as the view's `topMargin`, and re-enable
both tests.

[Webium] Pass profile-dependent omnibox popup values to each frame

A WebUIDataSource belongs to a BrowserContext, so in
TopChromeWebUIProfile, it is shared by the windows of all profiles. It
must not have values that depend on the profile of a window.

OmniboxPopupUI::GetProfileLoadTimeData() returns the popup's values that
depend on the profile: the profile-dependent searchbox values and its
own ones, e.g. the AI mode button and the default search provider icon.
They are added to the data source as before, unless the data source is
shared. Then, WebUIRenderFrameCreated() passes them to each frame
instead, and the popup adds them to loadTimeData before creating its
elements.

Nothing changes unless the popup is in TopChromeWebUIProfile, which a
follow-up CL does.

[FSA] Validate StorageKey and origin when serializing handles

Previously, `FileSystemAccessContext::SerializeHandle()` did not take
the caller's `blink::StorageKey`, and `LocalFileData` in
`file_system_access.proto` did not record the owning `url::Origin` for
local (`kLocal`) or external (`kExternal`) handles. As a result, a
compromised renderer holding a foreign transfer token could serialize it
into its own IndexedDB bucket and deserialize it to obtain a token and
permission grants bound to the deserializing origin.

Fix this by:
1. Passing the bucket's `blink::StorageKey` to
   `FileSystemAccessContext::SerializeHandle()` and verifying
   `IsValidTransferToken()` in
   `FileSystemAccessManagerImpl::DidResolveForSerializeHandle()` before
   serializing.
2. Recording the non-opaque `url::Origin` in `LocalFileData` during
   serialization and verifying in
   `FileSystemAccessManagerImpl::DeserializeHandle()` that the
   serialized origin is present and matches `storage_key.origin()`.

ba3738b4c1bcacc7272b650ed3f1c8cf9e9c7766 [ diff ] 
ios: Use the system locale as content shell's application locale

This CL overrides ShellContentBrowserClient::GetApplicationLocale() on
iOS to return the system locale. ShellContentBrowserClient now has an
application_locale_storage_ member, an ApplicationLocaleStorage. On
the first call, GetApplicationLocale() creates it and initializes it
with l10n_util::GetLocaleOverride(). Every call then returns the locale
value stored in it.

To make the system locale available, ShellBrowserMainParts now calls
l10n_util::OverrideLocaleWithCocoaLocale() in
PreCreateMainMessageLoop() on iOS.

[Webium] Add only profile-independent searchbox values to WebUI toolbar

The WebUI toolbar will be created in TopChromeWebUIProfile, which is
shared by the windows of all profiles. A WebUIDataSource belongs to a
BrowserContext, so the toolbar's data source there will be shared by
the windows of all profiles too, and must not have values that depend
on the profile of a window.

- SearchboxHandler splits the values of GetWebUIDataSourceDict() into
  GetProfileIndependentWebUIDataSourceDict() and
  GetProfileDependentWebUIDataSourceDict(). Each takes only the options
  it uses, so the former doesn't get the per-profile ones.
- WebUIToolbarUI adds only the profile-independent values to its data
  source. The toolbar doesn't read the others, which also need the user
  prefs that TopChromeWebUIProfile doesn't have.

The toolbar uses only <cr-searchbox-input>, with <cr-searchbox-icon>,
for the text field of its location bar. They read only searchBoxHint,
isLensSearchbox, isTopChromeSearchbox and reportMetrics, which are all
profile-independent. The profile-dependent values, e.g. the keyword and
composebox settings, are read by the other searchbox elements, e.g. the
dropdown and the composebox, which the toolbar doesn't use.

Also, WebUIToolbarUI now sets isTopChromeSearchbox after the searchbox
values, which have overwritten it with false since
crrev.com/c/8192944. It sets reportMetrics to false instead of true,
which was also overwritten, since the toolbar doesn't set the names of
the searchbox paint metrics, and has no dropdown, which reports them.

Except for isTopChromeSearchbox, the toolbar reads the same values as
before. No WebUI is in TopChromeWebUIProfile yet.

Add IsShowingResults to ContextualTasksPanelController

Introduces IsShowingResults() to ContextualTasksPanelController to check
whether the contextual tasks side panel is currently open and displaying
results for the active tab.
 ContextualTasksSidePanelCoordinator implements this via
IsShowingLensResults() and IsShowingAimResults(), identifying active
results when:
- A contextual task is waiting for its search URL to load
- A valid non-AIM search results page (such as a Lens SRP) is loaded in
  the side panel
- An AIM page is loaded and is not in the zero state
Also extends SidePanelWebContentsObserver with a navigation callback
invoked when primary main frame navigations commit.

[WebNN] CoreML: Return early on lhs input error in elementwise binary

In GraphBuilderCoreml::AddOperationForElementwiseBinary(), visiting a
constant lhs_operand calls SetInputFromOperand(), which writes to
weights.bin via WeightsFileHandle::Write(). If that write fails,
WeightsFileHandle::has_error_ is set to true.

Previously, AddOperationForElementwiseBinary() stored the error in
set_input_error and continued to visit rhs_operand before checking for
an error. When rhs_operand was also a constant operand, visiting it
called WeightsFileHandle::Write() a second time and hit
CHECK(!has_error_ && !finalized_).

Use RETURN_IF_ERROR() directly on the lhs_operand and rhs_operand
std::visit() calls so that any error while setting the first operand
returns immediately.

Deflake SettingsTest.ToggleButton browser test

The "click on learn more link should not toggle the button" subtest
clicks a target="_blank" link whose relative URL, "www.google.com",
resolves to chrome://settings/www.google.com. Settings serves its main
page for unknown paths, so this loaded the full Settings app in a new
foreground tab. The test page was then in a background tab, which
delayed each remaining subtest by ~1s due to timer throttling. On
linux-js-coverage-rel, JS coverage was also collected for the new tab,
since coverage is collected for every page on the test loader's host.
All 4 flaky failures there in the past week timed out at 45s while
collecting coverage, after all 23 subtests had passed.

Prevent the link's default action in the test, as other Settings tests
already do, so that no new tab is opened.

Locally, with --devtools-code-coverage, coverage was collected for one
page instead of two, the coverage output shrank from 5.8 MB to 3.7 MB,
and the test took 2.5s instead of 3.2s on average over 5 runs.

[CrOS] Remove unused camera count observer in Privacy Hub

SetUpCameraCountObserver() creates a CameraPresenceNotifier at login
that connects to VideoCaptureService and polls GetSourceInfos() every
3 seconds for the entire session. However, its callback
CameraPrivacySwitchController::OnCameraCountChanged() only writes to
camera_count_, a private field that is never read anywhere.

Remove SetUpCameraCountObserver() and the unused OnCameraCountChanged()
and camera_count_ member.

3pp: Add a PGO'ed GraalVM native-image of javac to the JDK package

Converts third_party/jdk/3pp to 3pp.py, and on linux-amd64 also ships
bin/javac-graalvm (~33MB): a native-image of the JDK's own javac
(trained by compiling javac's sources), built with Oracle GraalVM + PGO.

* Uses this JDK's jdk.compiler (via --patch-module), and a patched
  jdk.internal.jrtfs.SystemImage so that java.home (which defaults to
  the binary's parent directory) is respected.
* The version hash includes graalvm.py and the GraalVM release, and a
  LINT.IfChange ensures the JDK and GraalVM major versions match.

javac-graalvm vs JVM javac (chrome_java's 836 compile_java actions):
* All outputs are byte-identical.
* 48-way parallel: ~105s -> ~18s
* chrome_java alone: 13.3s -> 12.05s (GraalVM CE native-image: 15.5s)

Construct content_node_ids_ as base::flat_set<ui::AXNodeID> in Reset()

Replaces several usages of StrCat()/operator+ combined with
String::Number() with the more idiomatic Format() utility.

Using Format() is preferred in these cases as it:
1. Improves code readability.
2. Typically produces smaller and faster binary code.

This CL has no user-visible behavior changes.

[Media] Rename D3D texture wrapper files

The wrapper is no longer limited to D3D11 as resource handling expands
to D3D12. Use D3D-generic filenames so new resource implementations do
not inherit a D3D11-specific file name.

The roadmap for this file is as follows:
1. File rename (this CL)
2. Rename Texture2DWrapper to something like D3DResourceWrapper, and
rename DefaultTexture2DWrapper to DefaultD3DResourceWrapper or similar
3. Add D3D12 code, e.g. creating the DXGISharedHandleState and creating
the shared image from the D3D12 resource.

Eventually we will add a D3D12 version of CopyingTexture2DWrapper.

[Dse] Fix the 3P AI Mode button favicon blurry issue.

The 3P DSE's AI Mode button favicon was fetched without a desired size.
For a multi-resolution favicon such as an .ico, WebImage::FromData()
then decodes the smallest frame (e.g. 16x16), which is scaled up to the
24dp button icon and renders blurry.

In this CL, we request the favicon at the size it is displayed at, so
that the closest frame which is at least that large is decoded instead.
The decoded frame is then resized to that size, so large favicons (e.g.
1024x1024) aren't kept as multi-megabyte bitmaps.

Screenshots: http://shortn/_HH2Mw44o2D

[media] Preserve current_sequence_header_ across AV1Decoder::Reset()

`AV1Decoder::Reset()` previously cleared `current_sequence_header_`
while keeping the configured stream dimensions and profile, so the first
sequence header after a seek bypassed `RequiresHardwareContextReset()`.
Track whether a post-reset sequence header is needed via
`need_sequence_header_` while keeping `current_sequence_header_` for
comparison.

parent
1947c9bac747fcd3f5c873e565d5bdc2e6828c71 [ diff ] 
[ChroMenu] Keep menu open for zoom in/out search results

In the regular app menu, zoom in/out are inline buttons in
AppMenuZoomView that invoke their action directly, so the menu stays
open and the user can zoom repeatedly. In search results the same
actions are rendered as standard menu rows, so activating them went
through MenuController::Accept() and dismissed the menu after a single
step.

Add an AppMenuActionItem::kPersistsMenuKey property
(ActionParams::persists_menu), set it on kActionZoomMinus and
kActionZoomPlus, carry it through the search index onto the search
result items, and override
views::MenuDelegate::ShouldExecuteCommandWithoutClosingMenu() in
ActionAppMenu to honor it. Flagged rows now execute without closing the
menu for mouse, touch and keyboard activation; all other rows are
unchanged. The inline zoom buttons never consult the delegate, so their
behavior is unaffected.

parent
b98a7c3317f36c77f191810cec720582301d856c [ diff ] 
SuperSize: Lazily sort DeltaSizeInfo.symbols and avoid clustering on save

1. In diff.Diff and models.DeltaSizeInfo, defer clustering, alias
   grouping, and sorting of DeltaSizeInfo.symbols until .symbols is
   accessed, rather than computing it eagerly inside diff.Diff(...,
   sort=True) even when callers only use .raw_symbols or
   SaveDeltaSizeInfo(). Also invalidate cached _symbols in
   MergeDeltaSizeInfo() and MakeSparse() [C: diff.py:179-189,
   models.py:485-586].
2. In console._Session._SaveSizeInfo and _SaveDeltaSizeInfo, check
   raw_symbols with startswith('clank') instead of accessing
   size_info.symbols.WherePathMatches('^clank'), avoiding full symbol
   clustering and regex scanning across all symbols just to format the
   upload hint [C: console.py:207-225].

Expected speed-up: ~13.3s on create_patched_supersize_diff.py (9.1s in
first Diff, 1.0s in second Diff, and 3.2s in _SaveDeltaSizeInfo) [E].

Remove wexit_time_destructors config from //gpu

Since is_wexit_time_destructors_default is enabled by default for
Chromium builds, -Wexit-time-destructors is already part of
//build/config/compiler:default_warnings. This makes
//build/config/compiler:wexit_time_destructors a no-op. Remove all
redundant references to wexit_time_destructors in //gpu BUILD.gn files.

[contextual-tasks] Restore ABA search journeys in the side panel

When the user accepts the ABA Search Journeys cue on the tab they
returned to (Tab A), Chrome opens the Contextual Tasks side panel next
to it with the AI Overview they saw in Tab B, restored as the first
turn of an AI Mode thread. This adds that action, and a check the cue
can use to decide whether to show.

- SearchJourneyTracker::GetRestorableJourney() returns Tab A's journey
  only if it hasn't expired, Tab A is still on the page the user left,
  and the results page registered restore parameters.
- BuildRestoreUrl() builds the AI Mode URL from the default AI page
  URL, the search terms Chrome extracted from the results page as `q`,
  the restore parameters and `aep=228`. Query hints are never added.
- SearchJourneyTabFeature::RestoreJourneyInSidePanel() opens the side
  panel next to Tab A without adding Tab A as context, so it shows as
  the suggested tab. The journey is then dropped so it can't be
  restored twice.
- SearchJourneyTabFeature::CanRestoreJourneyInSidePanel() returns
  whether RestoreJourneyInSidePanel() would open the side panel now:
  the journey is restorable, Tab A is active, and contextual tasks
  entry points are eligible. Both functions share these checks, so
  the cue only shows when clicking it opens the side panel.

[webapps] Reject invalid document_url in ParseManifestFromString [2/N]

Validate that document_url is valid and has a non-opaque origin in
`ManifestManagerHost::ParseManifestFromString()` before dispatching the
ParseManifestFromString Mojo IPC to the renderer.

Previously, ParseManifestFromString() forwarded any browser-supplied
document_url to the renderer's ManifestParser, which falls back to
document_url for start_url. Once intrinsic manifest validation runs in
Mojo StructTraits::Read(), an invalid or opaque-origin document_url
would cause a benign renderer to return an invalid start_url or opaque
origin and get terminated. Reject invalid or opaque-origin document_url
inputs early by posting an empty manifest response asynchronously
without contacting the renderer.

[svg] Relayout an embedded SVG document's root when its frame is resized

The root of an SVG document inside <object>, <embed>, or a
RemoteFrameOwner takes the size of its frame. These SVG roots are
identified by IsEmbeddedThroughFrameContainingSVGDocument() and sized
in ComputeReplacedSize().

However, the SVG root's own height is still used to decide whether its
cached layout can be reused. When that height is a fixed length, for
example height="50", the cached layout will still be reused after the
height of the frame changes, and the root will keep its old height
instead of adapting to the new size of its frame.

Changes in width are already handled because the width is recomputed
on every resize.

Make SizeMayChange() return true for SVG roots embedded through a
frame, so that their size is recomputed whenever the frame is resized.

Tests:
  /wpt/svg/coordinate-systems/outer-svg-resize-001e.html
  /wpt/svg/coordinate-systems/outer-svg-resize-001o.html

Copy ListedElements before iterating in ConstructEntryList

HTMLFormElement::ConstructEntryList and BuildSearchString iterate over
ListedElements() while calling AppendToFormData() on each control. For
<textarea>, AppendToFormData() forces a synchronous style and layout
update, which can mutate the DOM and clear listed_elements_ mid-loop.
Copy ListedElements() before iterating, matching HTMLFormElement::reset
and the HTML specification.

Also guard ImageInputType::EnsurePrimaryContent() with InStyleRecalc(),
matching ImageInputType::SetUseFallbackContent(), so synchronous cached
image completion during layout tree attachment does not mutate the UA
shadow tree during style recalc.

WebTransport: implement GetStats for SendGroup

Replace zeroed send group statistics with aggregated bytes written,
sent, and acknowledged for the group's members. Snapshot membership when
getStats() is called so later reassignment does not change which streams
contribute to the pending result.

Track membership changes and fold finalized stream counters into group
totals, preserving statistics without retaining completed streams.

Request statistics for all active members in a single network-service
IPC. Share pending requests between stream and group queries, and keep
requests pending when statistics are temporarily unavailable until a
terminal notification or connection cleanup completes them.

[omnibox] Share the FocusToCutOrCopyAllTextTime logging

Problem: OmniboxPopupHandler::OnCutOrCopy() carries its own copy[1][2]
of LogOmniboxFocusToCutOrCopyAllTextTime() and LogHistogramMediumTimes()
from omnibox_view_views.cc[3]. The two can drift.

Fix: Move the function to omnibox::LogFocusToCutOrCopyAllTextTime() in
omnibox_logging_utils, alongside omnibox::LogFocusToOpenTime()[4] and
the shared LogHistogramMediumTimes() helper[5], and call it from both
omniboxes. Both duplicate LogHistogramMediumTimes() definitions are
removed[1][3][6].

Safe: No behavior change. Histogram names, buckets, and slicing are
unchanged. Both old copies log the same names, with the same 10 ms to
3 min range in 50 buckets, sliced the same way by page context and by
zero or typed suggest[1][2][3][5]. The copy came from an earlier CL[7].

Tests: 62/62 unit tests and 2/2 interactive tests passed.

[Masonry] Rename FlexColumnBreakInfo to ColumnBreakInfo

Column grid-lanes containers fragment each column independently, in the
same way as column flex containers. To handle fragmentation-driven item
expansion, forced breaks, and early breaks, grid-lanes needs the same
per-column tracking of intrinsic block size, break-after values, and
early breaks that `FlexColumnBreakInfo` already provides for flex.

This change renames `FlexColumnBreakInfo` to `ColumnBreakInfo`, and the
related `flex_column_break_info` parameters in the fragmentation
utilities and flex layout algorithm to `column_break_info`, so that
grid-lanes can reuse the struct in a follow-up change.

There is no change in behavior.

[AIM]: Use flex instead of absolute positioning in the AIM button

Typing the first character switches the pill from EXIT to SEND. Swapping
the icons must not make the label jump or move the pill and the mic next
to it. Flex transitions keep the pill width and the 18px label slide
without positioning anything manually.

Both icons stay in the DOM and transition width, margin and opacity. A
collapsed icon keeps a 4px margin, so the label stays 12px from the edge
whose icon is collapsed. The outgoing icon hides immediately; the
incoming one is revealed by its growing box while it fades in, instead
of fading in at full size.

Check menu() in AppMenu::ZoomView::UpdateFullScreenButton()

Entering immersive fullscreen synchronously closes and destroys AppMenu
while MenuController::OnMouseReleased() defers MenuRunnerImpl and
ZoomView destruction on the stack. Subsequent fullscreen layout calls
Widget::OnSizeConstraintsChanged(), invoking UpdateFullScreenButton()
after AppMenuView::menu_ has been invalidated.

Return early in UpdateFullScreenButton() when menu() is null, matching
GetActiveWebContents().

[Reading mode PDFs] Extract line segments from page paths

Extract straight stroked line segments (such as table borders and column
dividers) from top-level path objects on a PDFium page. Skip curves,
zero-length segments, non-stroked paths, and transparent strokes.
Transform points by the object matrix and convert them to pixel
coordinates, so rotated lines are reported at their rendered angle.

`PDFiumPage` only reports the geometry. Classifying segments as
horizontal or vertical ruling lines is left to the heuristic tree
builder.

Follow-up CLs pass the segments to the accessibility tree for grid table
detection.

Update ICU4X to 2.4.0

Updates the ICU4X 2.x crates to 2.4.0 and icu_experimental to 0.7.0,
along with their utility and Diplomat dependencies:
- icu_* (2.2.0/2.2.1/2.3.1 -> 2.4.0), adding icu_locale_fallback and
  icu_locale_fallback_data 2.4.0
- icu_experimental / icu_experimental_data (0.5.0 -> 0.7.0)
- icu_pattern (0.4.2 -> 0.5.0)
- fixed_decimal (0.7.2 -> 0.7.3), ixdtf (0.6.6 -> 0.6.7),
  tinystr (0.8.4 -> 0.8.5), yoke (0.8.3 -> 0.8.4),
  zerovec (0.11.8 -> 0.11.9), zerovec-derive (0.11.6 -> 0.11.7)
- diplomat / diplomat_core (0.15.0 -> 0.17.0) and diplomat-runtime
  (0.15.2 -> 0.16.1, unified across icu_capi and temporal_capi)

Also adds a patch to harfrust 0.14.0 to relax its =2.2.0 version pin on
icu_properties and avoid the deprecated to_icu4c_value() method.

[protobuf] Add roll_protobuf.py plan subcommand

The earlier CLs in this stack added BuildPatchChain, CopyPreimageBlobs,
ApplyChainPatchThreeWay, and PlanRoll to dry-run a protobuf roll in
temporary git repositories and diff upstream's src/file_lists.cmake
against Chromium's GN files.

However, PlanRoll is not yet exposed on the command line or formatted as
a human-readable report, so a roller still has no CLI command to see
which of the 24 patches in patches/ will apply cleanly, which are
already upstream, which will conflict, and which upstream source files
were added or removed before modifying the checkout.

Add FormatRollPlanReport and the `roll_protobuf.py plan --to` subcommand
(with `--json` support), and document the workflow in README.chromium.
Against upstream main (`819751af`), `plan` classifies 13 patches as
CLEAN, 4 as EMPTY, and 7 as CONFLICT, and reports 12 added upstream
files.

[protobuf] Replay patch chains and diff file lists in PlanRoll

With BuildPatchChain, CopyPreimageBlobs, and ApplyChainPatchThreeWay
in place, `roll_protobuf.py` needs an orchestrator that runs a dry-run
roll from README.chromium's revision to a candidate upstream revision
without modifying the checkout.

Add RollPlan and PlanRoll, which build the patch chain on old
upstream, replay it onto the target revision in a second temporary
repository (committing CLEAN patches and resetting others), and diff
src/file_lists.cmake between the two versions via check_file_lists.py.

This completes the M2 `PlanRoll` library implementation; the final CL
in the stack adds the report formatter, `plan --to` CLI subcommand,
and README.chromium documentation.

dea5a88629e34467e9622eec61bcfcbf9bf1f345 [ diff ] 
base: harden some checks for readonly pickles

Pickles use DCHECKs to assert a lot of their invariants, which has a
few unfortunate consequences:

* Readonly pickles created with ::WithUnownedBuffer() are silently
  writeable in release builds
* Pickle::Pickle() will construct a Pickle in a too-small buffer and
  corrupt memory
* Pickle::Reserve() with sizes > 4GB will underflow arithmetic in a
  bunch of unwholesome ways and corrupt memory

None of these are security vulnerabilities per se but they are risky
behaviors for the API to have. This change fixes all of these (by
promoting DCHECKs to CHECKs) and adds a test to ensure that they are
correctly forbidden.

These risky behaviors were originally found by Gemini.

[remoting] Bind LocalInputMonitor caller_task_runner on StartMonitoring

This CL address the problem where the MacOS disconnect dialog is
hidden/shown inconsistently when it should be based on the
existence of local input.

On single-process hosts (such as macOS), LegacyInteractionStrategy and
Me2MeDesktopEnvironment are initialized with `caller_task_runner`
set to `network_task_runner`, while `DisconnectWindowMac` runs on
`ui_task_runner` via `HostWindowProxy`.

Because `LocalInputMonitor::Create` previously bound
`caller_task_runner_` at construction time on `network_task_runner`,
calling `StartMonitoring()` from `DisconnectWindowMac::Start()` on
`ui_task_runner` caused input callbacks (`OnLocalMouseEvent`,
`OnLocalKeyPressed`) and subsequent `auto_hide_timer_` tasks to run
on `ChromotingNetworkThread` instead of the Cocoa main thread. This
prevented the macOS disconnect window from reappearing on local
input or auto-hiding after initial mouse activity.

Update `LocalInputMonitorImpl` to capture `caller_task_runner_` via
`base::SingleThreadTaskRunner::GetCurrentDefault()` when
`StartMonitoring()` or `StartMonitoringForClientSession()` is called,
and remove the redundant `caller_task_runner` parameter from
`LocalInputMonitor::Create()`.

Fix flaky Unbounded browser test(s)

Previously, GTEST_SKIP() was called inside the void helper function
SkipTestsForUnsupportedPlatforms(). Because GTEST_SKIP() expands to a
return statement, it only returned from the helper function rather
than from SetUp(), allowing ContentBrowserTest::SetUp() to still
launch the browser process, create the ContentShell window, and
immediately tear it down on skipped platforms. On Android, this
immediate Activity startup and teardown raced with Surface
initialization in libgui.so and caused flaky segmentation faults.

Move the GTEST_SKIP() checks directly into
UnboundedElementBrowserTestBase::SetUp() before
ContentBrowserTest::SetUp() is called so skipped tests return early
without starting the browser.

Add process extractor data structures

Add process extractor scaffolding under
components/enterprise/connectors/core/reporting/:
- ProcessNode captures process_id, parent_process_id, executable_path,
  and script_path for each process node in the ancestor chain.
- ProcessTree holds the ordered sequence of ProcessNode entries
  (process_nodes) from the immediate external process up to the root
  ancestor (capped at kMaxProcessAncestryDepth = 16 nodes, with path
  lengths capped at kMaxProcessPathLength = 1024 bytes).
- Add unit tests in process_extractor_unittest.cc.

Fix SODA uninstall race with component installation

Enabling Live Caption or starting a preemptive download after SODA
expired caused MaybeUninstallSoda to post a BEST_EFFORT directory
deletion right before InstallSoda registered the components at
USER_VISIBLE priority, deleting the base SODA directories during
component unpacking.

Evaluate preemptive downloads before MaybeUninstallSoda, only uninstall
SODA when language packs were removed and no feature using SODA is
enabled, and clear kSodaBinaryPath on uninstall.

[test] Zero production observation and pacing delays in Actor tests

`//chrome/browser/actor` browser tests (`593` tests in `browser_tests`,
averaging `6.75s` per test and consuming `53.4` excess test-minutes)
currently run every tool action (`Click`, `Type`, `Navigate`, `Select`,
`Scroll`, `MoveMouse`, `DragAndRelease`) with production human-pacing
and observation delay defaults:

1. `kActorPageStabilityMinWait` (`1000ms`),
   `kActorPaintStabilityInitialPaintTimeout` (`1000ms`), and
   `kActorPaintStabilitySubsequentPaintTimeout` (`1000ms`) on
   `kActorPageStability` enforce 1s minimum waits after every renderer
   tool action (note that `page_stability_browsertest.cc` and
   `observation_delay_controller_browsertest.cc` already override
   `kActorPageStabilityMinWait` to `0ms`).
2. `kActorObservationDelayLcp` (`1000ms`) on `kActorObservationDelay`
   delays completion whenever `page_load_metrics` has not yet flushed a
   1s buffered LCP update to the browser process.
3. `kActorTypeToolObservationStartDelayDuration` (`1000ms`),
   `kActorTypeToolEnterDelayParam` (`600ms`), and
   `kGlicActorIncrementalTyping` (`25ms` keydown + `25ms` keyup per
   character) add multiple seconds of timer sleep to `TypeTool` tests.
4. `kGlicActorUiMagicCursor` animates cursor movement for `50-300ms` per
   action before executing the tool.
5. `ActorClickToolBrowserTest` configured a `200ms` `kActorClickDelay`
   in the shared base fixture for all ~100 click tests even though only
   `ClickTool_Delay` tests click delay duration.

Configure `0ms` stability/observation/typing delays and `1ms` magic
cursor duration in `ActorToolsTest` and
`ExecutionEngineOriginGatingBrowserTestBase`, and scope the explicit
`kActorClickDelay` override to `ClickTool_Delay` (subclasses that
explicitly test timeouts or delays override the relevant feature in
their own `ScopedFeatureList`). Locally, this reduces
`ActorClickToolBrowserTest.ClickTool_SentToElement` from `5208ms` to
`2279ms` (`-56.2%`) and
`ActorTypeToolBrowserTest.TypeTool_FollowByEnter` from `8946ms` to
`3838ms` (`-57.1%`).

[omnibox] Add interactive tests for Full WebUI popup input-row icon

End-to-end coverage for the input-row cr-searchbox-icon in the Full
WebUI omnibox popup previously existed only in Mocha unit tests with
stubbed searchbox page handlers and loadTimeData. Add interactive UI
tests in FullWebUIOmniboxInteractiveTest covering:

- InputIconOnNtpFocusShowsDefaultSearchProviderIcon: focusing the
  omnibox on the NTP displays the default search provider icon in the
  input row (catches regressions where NTP focus fails to clear
  unedited pageUrl or load the default search provider icon).
- InputIconOnPageFocusShowsPageFavicon: clicking the omnibox on an
  HTTPS page with a favicon loads and displays that page's favicon via
  chrome://favicon2/ in place of the generic page icon (catches
  regressions in plumbing the active tab's page URL to the popup on
  focus or rendering its loaded favicon).
- InputIconUpdatesWhileTyping: typing a search query after focusing a
  page with a favicon switches the input-row icon to the default search
  provider icon, and typing a URL switches it to the URL match's
  favicon (catches regressions where user input leaves the unedited
  pageUrl icon active or fails to update the icon for the default
  autocomplete match).
- InputIconUpdatesWhileArrowing: arrowing down from a default URL match
  to a search suggestion and back up updates the input-row icon to
  match the selected suggestion (catches regressions where arrowing
  through suggestions updates input text without updating the input-row
  icon's selected match binding).

[glic-si] Clean up GlicMetrics doc comments and declarations

Add comments for invocation_source_, onboarding_invocation_source_ and
fre_accepted_time_ describing when they are set or overwritten and
which metrics consume them, and fix stale comments in glic_metrics.h
(references to a nonexistent controller_ member, a nonexistent
`success` parameter, and outdated lifecycle descriptions). Remove the
never-defined StoreSourceId() declaration and the unused
scroll_attempt_count_ member. Also drop a stale TODO in the
GlicKeyedService constructor about not constructing GlicMetrics, which
still records profile-scoped metrics.

Also correct the Glic.Fre.UserInput.InvocationSource summary: the
recorded value is the invocation source of the most recent Glic open
before onboarding was accepted, not the last source before input.

No behavior change.

[iOS] Re-enable ClipboardJsTest read tests

Re-enable ClipboardJsTest.TestReadTextAndAllow and
ClipboardJsTest.TestReadAndAllow, which were conditionally disabled on
physical devices.

These tests were disabled on device in crrev.com/c/8376752 due to
failures on physical hardware (crbug.com/559140540). Subsequent fixes
to clipboard handling and user activation bypass in crrev.com/c/8405947
resolved the underlying issue. Both tests now pass 11/11 iterations on
the test runner.

[headless] Enable brotli compression for headless command resources

//components/headless/command_handler/BUILD.gn already sets `use_brotli
= true` on `headless_command_resources`, but `headless_command.grd`
omitted `compress="brotli"` on its `<include>` entries, causing grit to
fall back to default compression.

[Organizer] Lower debounce for organizer searches via search mixin

It turns out the search component has a debounce that ranges from 500ms
to 200ms and it is inversely proportional to the query length. The
current tab search has instant search and these queries shouldn't be
expensive so adding an override.

Remove wexit_time_destructors config from //cc

Since is_wexit_time_destructors_default is enabled by default for
Chromium builds, -Wexit-time-destructors is already part of
//build/config/compiler:default_warnings. This makes
//build/config/compiler:wexit_time_destructors a no-op. Remove all
redundant references to wexit_time_destructors in //cc. Note that //cc
test code already specify no_exit_time_destructors, so this CL is just
stopping the tug-o-war.
